# BuildLang

> BuildLang (`buildc v1.15.0`) is a deterministic systems and GPU language whose function signatures declare capabilities (`~ Console + FileSystem + Network + Foreign`). `buildc check` rejects undeclared capability use and reports stable `BLxxxx` diagnostics in JSON. It compiles across 12 CPU and GPU targets (`c`, `llvm`, `x86-64`, `arm64`, `riscv64`, `wasm`, `spirv`, `hlsl`, `glsl`, `msl`, `wgsl`, `rust`) and ships BuildDB (`qdb`), BuildTeX (`typeset`), and the `port` migration tool.

Agents writing BuildLang: run `buildc check FILE --error-format=json` after every edit, read each diagnostic's `code`, `help`, and `suggestions`, and never apply a suggestion marked `widens_authority` unless that capability belongs on the function.

## Install

- Windows (PowerShell, SHA-256 verified): `irm https://raw.githubusercontent.com/HarperZ9/buildlang/main/install.ps1 | iex`
- Linux and macOS (SHA-256 verified): `curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/HarperZ9/buildlang/main/install.sh | sh`
- From crates.io: `cargo install buildlang`

## Verified Capabilities

- Certified V5 e-graph superoptimizer (`--superopt`, `--emit-cert`, `buildc verify-cert`, PR #344): deterministic MIR saturation across 13 integer and IEEE-754 rules with independent fail-closed axiom checking across all 12 targets.
- Certified GPU polyhedral loop tiling and uniformity-safe subgroup translation validation (`--emit-gpu-cert`, `--subgroup-mode`, `buildlang.gpu-tv-cert/v1`, PR #346): checks RAW/WAR loop-carried dependences and divergent barriers fail-closed across `wgsl`, `hlsl`, `msl`, and `spirv`.
- Universe and stdlib status (PR #347): `113/276` universe modules pass `buildc check` (`universe/CHECK-FAILS.txt` reduced from `170` to `163`, `0` regressions), and Tier-1 organism component `universe/foundation` compiles and passes under MSVC.
- Storage, typesetting, and migration: BuildDB/BuildQL (`bdb/db.bld`, format 2 per-4-KiB FNV-1a page checksums, `0/500` silent fuzz corruptions), BuildTeX (`typeset/`, zero external TeX binaries), and `port` (`port c`, `port py`, `port plain`, plus `port/universal/` lifters).
